children: The Indian rupee opened lower against the US dollar on September 11, with the oil rally gathering pace, pushing U.S. Treasury yields higher and fuelling risk aversion.
The rupee opened 24 paise weak at 95.68 per dollar, compared with Thursday’s close of 95.44.
According to Finrex, rupee is set to open at 99.69 with 99.75 as a resistance which RBI was constantly protecting last month.
The US Yields moved higher and so was Brent at $ 107.53. Accordingly, the dollar Index was also higher at 99.03 while Asian currencies fell along with Equities.
Let’s see if RBI protects today the level of 95.75 or we move higher on the pair. Exporters can continue to sell at 99.75 while importers to buy the dips, it added.
Asian currencies traded mixed against the US dollar, with the South Korean won leading gains, rising 0.32%, followed by the Singapore dollar and Japanese yen, which strengthened 0.06% each.

On the other hand, the Philippine peso fell 0.34%, while the Taiwan dollar, Malaysian ringgit and Indonesian rupiah declined 0.24%, 0.22% and 0.21%, respectively. The Chinese renminbi and Thai baht also weakened marginally.

The dollar held near its highest levels of the past week and the yen slipped for a second day at the start of Asian trading on Friday as renewed fears of energy supply disruptions in the Middle East pushed up bond yields and oil prices.

title: Currency Check: Rupee opens 24 paise lower at 95.68/$ as oil prices rise
